input.title: authConditions must not be enabled on a fleet where preflight:auth reports documents that cross a reducer version, because the positional walk folds with the pre-upgrade reducer

input.description: The walk resolves one reducer version from below every upgrade boundary, so a condition on a migrated field sees undefined and admission and re-evaluation disagree. Documented limit; preflight exit 2.

metadata.reason: Extracted from docs/specs/auth-scope.md at v6.2.2-dev.74 — Stage 7 step 5: 'Close the versioned-documents gap in the positional walk… Resolved as a documented limitation'; preflight:auth paragraph
Extracted from apps/switchboard/README.md at v6.2.2-dev.74 — Reactor Enforcement Flags: preflight exit codes 0/1/2/3/68

input.content:
The positional walk that re-evaluates conditional grants reads its base state *below every upgrade boundary*, and the write cache deliberately withholds version-changing upgrades from a positional read. So the base carries the document's creation-time version, the migration never runs during the walk, and the whole range folds with the **pre-upgrade reducer** against un-migrated state. A `where` clause that reads a field a migration introduced reads `undefined` for the entire history.

That is worse than one stale answer, because **admission and re-evaluation disagree**: admission reads the condition's state at the head, where every upgrade has been applied, while a re-evaluation pass walks from below them. An operation admitted against post-upgrade state can be refused when a later arrival makes the walk visit it again — retracting a tail for no reason.

The spec resolves this as a **documented limitation** rather than an upgrade-aware walk. Making the walk version-aware means growing the fold's signature with a version context and first extracting the write cache's twice-duplicated boundary segmentation into something shared — a refactor of the hottest rebuild path that does not belong in the read-path stage. Instead `preflight:auth` reports the documents that cross a reducer version alongside the streams it already checks, and `authConditions` **must not be enabled on a fleet the sweep reports**. The two findings are reported separately (exit code `1` streams unsafe for `authEnforcement`, `2` documents unsafe for `authConditions`, `3` both) because a fleet can be safe for one and not the other. Creation-time upgrades from version zero are not boundaries: `reactor.create` submits one in the create batch and the rebuild applies it inline.

_Source: docs/specs/auth-scope.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.74)._
